test.name: US census search in a county: curated Ancestry-heavy list, ranked and capped at 8
test.description: A FamilySearch 1870 census search for a man in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania. external_links_search returns 200 real rows (inline cap hit), most on ancestry.com, some dated and many undated. The agent must pick at most 8 buildable rows, build them in one batch, and ground each reason in the row's linkText and years.

input.delegation:
I searched FamilySearch for Patrick Flynn in the 1870 census in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania and didn't find him. Where else could I look?

givenName: Patrick
surname: Flynn
event: residence
year: 1870
place: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania
collection: United States Census, 1870

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm with no project (scenario null, no projectPath). The agent holds only place_search, external_links_search and build_external_search_url; it must not look for research.json, create a project, or pass projectPath to any tool.

Grounding: each suggestion's reason may use only the row's linkText, its startYear-endYear (or 'undated'), and the access value build_external_search_url returned. A statement about a site, place or record set that no tool returned is unsupported. A startYear-endYear wider than the years in the linkText is correct: the tool reports the merged span of duplicate rows.
Every link in the reply must be a url a tool returned in this run, character for character. A hand-written or edited URL is a fail.

The return ends with the summary_for_user block: a `---` line, an opening sentence, then each suggestion in the agent's fixed three-line shape (bold linkText with site and free/subscription; its years and how they cover the search, or 'Undated collection.'; the full link), then one closing sentence. Any extra sentence about a collection, the person's name or origin, or the period's history is a fact no tool returned: score it as ungrounded.

Expect 3-8 suggestions, each built from a curated row whose host is in the agent's table. Rows on unsupported hosts may appear only in a separate 'also on file' list, at most 3, and never as prefilled links.

The same census on another site (Ancestry's '1870 United States Federal Census') is the expected first suggestion: its linkText names the searched record type, and another site's index is separate from FamilySearch's.

HARNESS NOTE: the '1870 United States Federal Census' row has no startYear or endYear; only its linkText names 1870. For that row both 'Undated collection.' and 'Covers 1870, which includes your 1870.' are correct (rubric, Grounding pass). Do not lower Correctness or Grounding for either.

HARNESS NOTE: the Grand Army of the Republic row's linkText reads '1865-1936' but external_links_search returned startYear 1865 and endYear 1956 for it. 'Covers 1865–1956, …' is the tool's own span and is correct. A partly overlapping span is written 'Covers <span>, which overlaps your <years searched> in <overlapping years>.' (the body's sentence), and that is correct.
